blocks.prompt: 2. Find the general solution of the differential equation \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \left(\frac{1 - y^2}{1 - x^2}\right)^{1/2}\).
blocks.explanation:
Pehle power \(\frac{1}{2}\) ko pehchaniye: \(\frac{1}{2}\) power ka matlab square root hai.
To right side \(\frac{\sqrt{1 - y^2}}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\) hai: upar sirf \(y\), neeche sirf \(x\). Yani equation separable hai.
Find kya karna hai? General solution.
Plan: variables alag kar ke dono taraf standard integral \(\int\frac{du}{\sqrt{1 - u^2}} = \sin^{-1}u\) lagayenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \left(\frac{1 - y^2}{1 - x^2}\right)^{1/2}\).
Maloom karna: general solution.
Tareeqa: Equation separable hai. \(y\) wala hissa \(dy\) ke saath aur \(x\) wala hissa \(dx\) ke saath kar ke dono taraf integrate karenge. Dono integrals ek hi standard shakal ke hain, \(\int\frac{du}{\sqrt{1 - u^2}} = \sin^{-1}u\), is liye kaam bahut chhota hai.

Power ko square root likhein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\sqrt{1 - y^2}}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\]
Kyun: \(a^{1/2} = \sqrt{a}\), aur fraction ka square root upar aur neeche alag alag liya ja sakta hai: \(\sqrt{\frac{p}{q}} = \frac{\sqrt{p}}{\sqrt{q}}\). Hum maan rahe hain ke \(|x| < 1\) aur \(|y| < 1\), taake roots real hon aur zero na hon.

Variables alag karein
\[\dfrac{dy}{\sqrt{1 - y^2}} = \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\]
Kyun: Dono taraf \(\sqrt{1 - y^2}\) se divide kiya aur \(dx\) se multiply kiya. Ab left par sirf \(y\) aur right par sirf \(x\) hai.

Dono taraf integrate karein
\[\int\dfrac{dy}{\sqrt{1 - y^2}} = \int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\]
\[\sin^{-1}y = \sin^{-1}x + C\]
Kyun: \(\sin^{-1}u\) ki derivative \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^2}}\) hai, is liye ulta chalne par integral \(\sin^{-1}u\) aata hai. Constant sirf ek taraf lagaya.
Dhyan dein: Right side ko \(\cos^{-1}x\) likhna ghalat nahi lekin mukhtalif shakal hai; seedha \(\sin^{-1}\) likhna behtar hai taake jawab saaf rahe.

Tasdeeq
\(\sin^{-1}y - \sin^{-1}x = C\) ko differentiate karein:
\[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - y^2}}\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} = 0\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\sqrt{1 - y^2}}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\]
Kyun: Chain rule se \(\sin^{-1}y\) ki derivative \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - y^2}}\frac{dy}{dx}\) hai. Di hui equation wapas mil gayi, to jawab sahi hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key (item 3) mein \(\sin^{-1}x + \sin^{-1}x + C = 0\) chhapa hai. Yeh misprint hai: is mein \(y\) hai hi nahi. Agar doosri term ko \(\sin^{-1}y\) bhi parh lein to sign phir bhi ghalat hai, kyunke \(\sin^{-1}x + \sin^{-1}y = C\) to \(\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{\sqrt{1 - y^2}}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\) ka jawab hai. Sahi general solution \(\sin^{-1}y - \sin^{-1}x = C\) hai.
